title = "The Ungrateful Trainees (1)"

<p>“Haa…! Hah…!”</p><p>“Seo-eun, let’s end your personal training here for today.”</p><p>“Y-Yes…! Phew… Thank you…”</p><p>As usual, I trained with Seo-eun today. Since Min Se-rin wasn’t around for the month and my evenings were free, I decided to take on a few extra trainees from the applicants for additional training sessions.</p><p>The applicants trained together in the evening, and after that, I held personal training sessions with Seo-eun.</p><p>I told Seo-eun she could train with the other applicants, but she insisted she wanted to stick with one-on-one training like always. Impressed by her dedication, I pushed her even harder than before.</p><p>‘Huh, she’s more eager to train than I thought…’</p><p>Throughout the session, Seo-eun’s face clearly showed she didn’t want to train, but once we started, she followed every instruction without complaint.</p><p>“Hwaa…”</p><p>Seo-eun, who had been sprawled on the floor, managed to regain some strength. She wobbled to her feet and plopped down beside me, then started chugging my water.</p><p>‘Wait… She’s been doing this since last time—never brings her own water bottle and just drinks mine…’</p><p>As if it didn’t matter that I’d drunk from it, she pressed her lips to the bottle and gulped it all down in one go before hurling the empty plastic bottle toward the trash can.</p><p>Thunk.</p><p>“Ah!”</p><p>But the bottle didn’t make it in. It hit the rim, bounced off, and rolled across the floor.</p><p>I stared at Seo-eun in disbelief.</p><p>“Are you sure you’re an Awakened? Even my college-aged little sister could make that shot…”</p><p>Seo-eun’s face flushed red at my expression and the mention of my sister. She snapped back,</p><p>“W-What? I can do it blindfolded normally! My hands are just too weak right now!”</p><p>“Sure, whatever.”</p><p>I knew she was telling the truth. Her hands had been shaking ever since she grabbed the water bottle. After gripping a dual-bladed training sword nonstop for over two hours without a single break, that was only natural.</p><p>I’d just wanted to tease her a little, so I’d put on an exaggerated look of shock.</p><p>“Where did you go for your mission this time?”</p><p>“I went to Japan.”</p><p>“No way… Japan? Did you go with the Association President?”</p><p>“Yeah, something like that.”</p><p>“A-rank Hunters really are different. What did you do there?”</p><p>“What else? It was a bodyguard mission, so I did bodyguard work.”</p><p>As the days of training passed, Seo-eun and I had started exchanging a few words after sessions, but this was the first time our conversation had gone on this long.</p><p>I wasn’t sure if it was because she was happy to see me after weeks apart, or if she actually wanted to quit the personal training but couldn’t bring herself to say it and was just making small talk. But one thing was clear—her attitude was warmer than usual.</p><p>“…Instructor, you have a sister?”</p><p>“Yeah.”</p><p>“How old are you?”</p><p>“Twenty-three.”</p><p>“Wow, we’re the same age?”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>Seo Eun looked at me with a playful grin, as if she found it amusing that she and Ji-hyeon were the same age as me.</p><p>“Aren’t you sorry for treating a girl the same age as your little sister so harshly?”</p><p>“Well… my little sister is kind, hardworking, cute, smart, and doesn’t play tricks. So I’ve never gotten mad at her or made her do anything like training.”</p><p>“Unbelievable.”</p><p>Seo Eun muttered in disbelief at my idiotic answer, fidgeting with her hands.</p><p>“I’m jealous.”</p><p>“About what?”</p><p>“If my brother were an A-rank Hunter, I’d get a lot of allowance, live without money worries, and go to college happily.”</p><p>Honestly, she wasn’t wrong. I did give her allowance sometimes, paid for her outings, and even covered her rent and tuition. So I had no comeback.</p><p>‘Maybe I should head back to my room and handle some paperwork…’</p><p>“Then I should—”</p><p>As I tried to get up, Seo Eun grabbed the hem of my clothes.</p><p>“Do you have something to say…?”</p><p>“Uh…”</p><p>Seo Eun, still holding my clothes, tilted her head back to look up at me and said,</p><p>“For this mission… you were supposed to go to the Gate as a supervisor with us, right?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I didn’t know where she was going with this, but standing there with my clothes grabbed felt awkward, so I sat back down on the bench to hear her out.</p><p>“So… you know about the tradition where the instructor in charge takes the trainees to the Gate and then treats them to a meal afterward, right?”</p><p>“Ah.”</p><p>I’d forgotten, but I did know.</p><p>Technically, the special class didn’t have such traditions, but back when I was in the special class, I’d heard from my peers that in the regular classes, instructors would take their trainees to the Gate for practical training and then treat them to a big meal afterward. At the time, since instructors were seen as demonic figures who constantly tormented and beat us, my peers and I had dismissed the rumor with comments like, ‘They’re probably just stuffing us full so we’ll puke it all out in the next training session,’ or ‘They must be putting poison in the food to build our resistance.’</p><p>‘So that tradition really existed.’</p><p>Even though I hadn’t gone on the practical training myself, since it was my class, I figured it was only right to treat them to a meal.</p><p>“Then I’ll buy you all a meal… Do the trainees have anything specific they’d like to eat?”</p><p>“Really? Then I’ll ask them tomorrow. Since we have theory classes on the weekend, we’re stuck at the training center all week. How about Friday?”</p><p>“Sounds good.”</p><p>Seo Eun seemed satisfied with my answer. She dusted off her clothes a couple of times before standing up.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290904" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Well, thanks for today’s training. I’ll head out now. See you tomorrow!”</p><p>“Yeah.”</p><p>After that, Se-rin bowed her head to me and left the training grounds with light steps.</p><p>***</p><p>“So… that’s it for today.”</p><p>“Y-Yes… *huff*…!”</p><p>Another day passed, and just like yesterday, I held classes with the trainees in the morning and did personal training in the evening.</p><p>Despite my personal motto—“Training should be like real combat”—and the fact that I pushed them pretty hard, the number of trainees signing up for personal training kept increasing.</p><p>Seeing them diligently follow along with the training filled me with something like pride.</p><p>‘Is this how a teacher feels?’</p><p>In fact, after today’s class, one of the female trainees even asked why Se-rin got one-on-one training while the rest of the applicants had to train in a group.</p><p>Her tone carried a hint of jealousy, as if she saw one-on-one training as some kind of special privilege.</p><p>‘If they actually tried it, they’d regret it…’</p><p>“Phew… that hits the spot.”</p><p>As usual, Se-rin sat beside me, grabbed my water bottle without a second thought, chugged it all in one go, then tossed it toward the trash can.</p><p>Clunk.</p><p>“In!”</p><p>“…”</p><p>She made the shot—something she should’ve been able to do anyway—then looked at me with a smug, “How’s that?” expression.</p><p>It seemed my reaction from yesterday had stuck in her mind.</p><p>“Oh right! I asked the others, and we’re all eating at a meat restaurant this Friday!”</p><p>“Mm… did you pick a place?”</p><p>“Uh… what was the name again… There’s this huge three-story meat place a little ways into the city from the training academy… I made a reservation there.”</p><p>“Ah, I know the one. Then let’s meet there Friday evening.”</p><p>“Okay!”</p><p>It was a restaurant I’d seen on the drive to the training academy—a three-story place that looked expensive, high-end, and packed with customers. That was why it had stuck in my memory.</p><p>‘Well, if we’re fitting 30 people, it has to be that big. Even if it’s pricey, it’ll probably only come to two or three million won…’</p><p>“Oh, and the number of personal training applicants keeps going up. Starting tomorrow, what do you think about letting a few other female trainees join instead of just one-on-one? Some of them asked why only Se-rin gets one-on-one training…”</p><p>“Huh? No way!”</p><p>“…?”</p><p>Se-rin openly rejected the idea. Honestly, I’d assumed she’d be happy—adding more people would naturally lower the intensity of the training. But her unexpected reaction left me confused.</p><p>“Why not?”</p><p>“W-Well, that’s because… um…! One-on-one training lets you learn more, right?!”</p><p>“That’s unexpected…”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Nothing…”</p><p>I was surprised that Seo-eun had this much passion for training. If she was this determined, I thought I could increase the intensity starting tomorrow.</p><p>“You’re Yu Hyeon-jeong, right?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“The trainee who asked the instructor why only you were getting one-on-one training—Yu Hyeon-jeong, correct?”</p><p>“…”</p><p>She didn’t answer, but it was her. The two of them didn’t seem to get along—during training, they subtly exchanged barbs. Judging by Seo-eun’s reaction now, they really didn’t like each other.</p><p>“She’s been in close contact with the instructors for a while, meeting them privately and stuff. She probably brought it up because she wants to get closer to the instructor.”</p><p>“…”</p><p>‘That’s rich coming from you.’</p><p>Seo-eun’s response was openly hostile.</p><p>“I don’t know what happened between you two, but for now, let’s keep your training one-on-one, Seo-eun.”</p><p>“Y-Yes…”</p><p>Since I’d started one-on-one training to correct her habits, changing it now would be awkward… It’d be better to recommend that Yu Hyeon-jeong train with the other students.</p><p>“Then see you tomorrow.”</p><p>“Yes…! Thank you again for today!”</p><p>The mood turned strange when Yu Hyeon-jeong came up, so I quickly stood up to leave.</p><p>I still had work to do back in my room, plus calls with Yu-na and Ji-hyeon.</p><p>Somehow, evening calls with family had become part of my daily routine.</p><p>As I left the training grounds, lost in thought, I spotted a figure standing in front of my room door in the distance.</p><p>‘Se-rin? …No, not her.’</p><p>The person in the hallway was none other than Yu Hyeon-jeong, the trainee Seo-eun had just mentioned.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290905" loading="lazy"></p><p>‘She’s got some nerve too.’</p><p>“Instructor!”</p><p>Yu Hyeon-jeong waved at me as if she’d been waiting. Had she?</p><p>“Yes, what brings you here?”</p><p>“Well… I trained alone tonight, and I have some questions, so… could you spare a little time?”</p><p>“Huh? Uh, sure… Should we go to the lobby on the first floor?”</p><p>“No! You just finished personal training with Eun, right? You must be tired. Let’s just talk here instead of going down.”</p><p>“…”</p><p>What’s *your* deal?</p>
